os_source: EMMA EP378888 Official Statement dated 2017-08-16 (ER1077935-ER843996-ER1244777.pdf), cached at data/os_cache/050002AW4_OS.pdf
verdict_one_line: Essential-service FIRST-LIEN GROSS-revenue pledge with the strongest fund in a distressed city (Wastewater LENT to the General Fund, not vice-versa), ring-fenced and segregated, AGM-insured AA / BBB- underlying, ~1.3-1.5x net coverage well above the 120% covenant; buy as staged.
pledge: FIRST LIEN on GROSS Revenues of the Wastewater System (not net). Special limited obligation; payable SOLELY from Gross Revenues. NO general-fund backup, NO full faith & credit, no lien on physical assets, no tax pledge. O&M is paid as a junior application of pledged Gross Revenues, AFTER debt service in the flow of funds.
lien: Senior / first lien. On parity with the 2008 Installment Payments (2008 Bonds, $20,020,000). City may incur future parity or subordinate debt; covenants not to issue any debt SUPERIOR to the Bonds. One small subordinate lease (Vac-Con sewer cleaner) outstanding.
rate_covenant: NET Revenues >= 120% (1.20x) of Debt Service Payments on the Bonds and Parity Obligations each Fiscal Year (Indenture rate covenant, OS p.17). Note: the rate covenant is measured on NET revenues even though the LIEN is on gross. Cure provision: a one-year miss is not an Event of Default if the City re-complies at the start of the next FY.
dsrf: FUNDED via SURETY, not cash. A municipal bond debt-service Reserve Policy (Policy Limit $4,624,363.40) from AGM deposited at closing satisfies the Reserve Requirement. Reserve Requirement = least of (i) 10% of initial offering price, (ii) MADS, or (iii) 125% of average annual DS. Surety (not cash) is a mild credit minus vs a cash-funded reserve.
abt: Additional parity debt requires a CPA/Financial-Consultant certificate that historical NET Revenues for any 12 of the trailing 18 months were >= 120% of MAX annual debt service (pro forma, all parity post-issuance). Adjustable for Additional Revenues (rate increases adopted/effective within 18 mo, plus new connections). Refunding parity exempt from the test under stated conditions.
insurance: INSURED by Assured Guaranty Municipal Corp. (AGM). Reserve also surety-backed by AGM. At issuance: INSURED rating S&P 'AA'; UNDERLYING rating S&P 'BBB-'. AGM financial strength at issuance: S&P AA / KBRA AA+ / Moody's A2.
issue_price_this_maturity: PREMIUM. 2040 term (AW4) priced at 114.060%, yield 3.290%, priced to the 2027-05-01 optional call at par (the (C) yield-to-call convention).
oid: No OID for this maturity. Issued at a substantial PREMIUM (114.06), 5% coupon vs ~3.29% YTC. Premium / amortizable-bond-premium maturity, NOT a de-minimis or market-discount concern.
adverse_notes: CITY-LEVEL GOING-CONCERN HISTORY (honestly disclosed, but does NOT impair THIS pledge): the City declared a common-law fiscal emergency 2012-10-03, considered AB 506 / Chapter 9, and the FY2015-16 auditor carried a going-concern doubt for the GENERAL FUND and SANITATION ENTERPRISE FUND. KEY MODE-B FINDING: the WASTEWATER Fund is the city's STRONG fund -- it 'remained solvent throughout the City's other financial difficulties' and in July 2014 LENT money OUT to the distressed funds (Water $1.495M, Sanitation $4.189M, General Fund $2.966M @0.251%). Direction of stress is OUT of, not into, the pledged enterprise. The Bonds require NO GF advance and a Revenue-Fund segregation covenant (separate bank account by 2018-09-30, no commingling).

BBB- underlying = the bond is investment-grade but at the bottom rung WITHOUT the wrap; the AA rating is AGM-dependent. Wrap value is real here (rating-conditional wrap compression: BBB- underlying is exactly where AGM insurance buys the most spread compression).
DSRF is a SURETY (AGM policy), not cash -- reserve quality is only as good as AGM.

WHOLESALE-CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION: ~$2.37M/yr (~20% of charges) from 3 wholesale contracts -- Winton Sanitary District, U.S. Penitentiary, Castle Airport; a meter failure already cut Castle revenue in FY15-16. Federal (USP) and special-district customers are sticky but concentrated.

PROP 218 (Art. XIIIC/XIIID) constrains rate-setting: wastewater charges are property-related, subject to majority-protest process; Art. XIIIC initiative power could theoretically reduce rates (Govt Code 5854 offers some debt-service protection but is untested in court). Standard for CA water/sewer; not idiosyncratic.
MODEST CONNECTION-FEE DEPENDENCE but NOT load-bearing: connection-fee revenue is small ($13k-$346k/yr) relative to ~$11-12M service charges; coverage does not hinge on new connections.

Rate increases are CPI-indexed (small: 0% / 1% / 0% recent years); Atwater's $71.96 avg monthly bill is already ~2-3x neighboring cities (Fresno $25.75, Modesto $33.76), limiting headroom for large future increases.

coverage_context.note: Historical net coverage ~1.32-1.46x sits comfortably above the 1.20x covenant; the refunding lowered debt service so projected coverage rises to ~1.6x. Wastewater Fund carries a >2-year O&M operating reserve.

basis: Read of the actual EMMA Official Statement (dated 2017-08-16) cover + inside cover (pp.1-2), SECURITY FOR THE BONDS / Rate Covenant / Reserve Fund / Parity Obligations (pp.14-20 [OS pagination] = PDF pp.22-28), Bond Insurance & Ratings (pp.22-23, 64 = PDF pp.30-31, 72), Wastewater operations / wholesale customers / rates / connection fees (pp.35-39 = PDF pp.43-47), coverage tables 11-12 (pp.43-45 = PDF pp.51-53), Going Concern & Inter-fund Transfers + Risk Factors / Prop 218 (pp.48-49, 53-56 = PDF pp.56-57, 61-64).

thesis_check.essential_service_net_revenue_pledge: PARTIALLY CORRECT / STRONGER THAN ASSUMED. Essential-service: YES. But the pledge is on GROSS revenues with a FIRST lien (a stronger structure than a net-revenue pledge); only the rate COVENANT is measured on net revenues.
thesis_check.approx_1_2x_rate_covenant: CONFIRMED. Exactly 1.20x net revenues / debt service.
thesis_check.standard_structure: MOSTLY CONFIRMED, with two non-standard items to flag: (1) DSRF is a surety, not cash; (2) the issuer city carries a disclosed GENERAL-FUND going-concern history -- but the pledged enterprise is the city's solvent, net-lender fund and is ring-fenced, so the city distress does not flow through to this lien.

quotes: Debt Service Payments are a special limited obligation of the City, payable from and secured by a pledge of and first lien on all Gross Revenues (defined herein) of the City's wastewater collection, treatment and disposal system. (OS cover, p.1)
This pledge shall constitute a first lien on the Gross Revenues for the payment of the Debt Service Payments and debt service on any Parity Obligations in accordance with the Indenture. (OS p.14)

the City will fix and prescribe rates and charges for the Wastewater System which are reasonably expected to be at least sufficient to yield during each Fiscal Year Net Revenues equal to 120% of Debt Service Payments on the Bonds and Parity Obligations for such Fiscal Year (OS Rate Covenant, p.17)
On the Closing Date, the Reserve Policy, with a Policy Limit of $4,624,363.40, will be deposited into the Reserve Fund, which shall satisfy the Reserve Requirement. (OS Reserve Fund, p.18)

the Net Revenues ... for any 12 consecutive calendar months during the 18 calendar month period ... shall have amounted to at least 120% of the Maximum Annual Debt Service for all Bonds or Parity Obligations to be outstanding immediately after incurring such additional Bonds or Parity Obligations. (OS Future Parity Obligations, p.19)
RATINGS: Insured: S&P: 'AA' / Underlying: S&P: 'BBB-' ... guaranteed under a municipal bond insurance policy ... by Assured Guaranty Municipal Corp. (the 'Insurer' or 'AGM'). (OS cover, p.1)
$8,945,000 5.000% Term Bonds Due May 1, 2040; Price - 114.060%(C); Yield - 3.290%; CUSIP - AW4 ... (C) Priced to optional redemption date of May 1, 2027 at par. (OS inside cover, p.2)

In an action that strengthened the Wastewater Fund, which fund had remained solvent throughout the City's other financial difficulties ... In July 2014, the City Council approved three inter-fund loans FROM the Wastewater Fund [to Water, Sanitation, and the General Fund]. (OS p.49)
The City will not be required to advance any moneys derived from the General Fund or any other source of income other than Gross Revenues ... for the payment of the Debt Service Payments. (OS p.49)

the Auditor continued to assume that there was substantial doubt that the City would be able to continue as a going concern because the General Fund and Sanitation Enterprise Fund each continued to suffer recurring deficits from operations. (OS Going Concern, p.48)
